messages:
alex: Quick snapshot — ran a multi-pop latency stitch for Llama3-xl int8 across US-E / US-W / EU-C. Edge proxy fanout=2, kernel=opt-attn-v2, batch=8, KV-cache=on, warmup=on. Uniform 1k reqs/region. Results (p50 / p95) below.

alex: ```
US-E (h100 int8)   : p50 45ms  p95 120ms
US-W (a100 int8)   : p50 70ms  p95 260ms  <-- outlier
EU-C (h100 int8)   : p50 55ms  p95 140ms
```

maria: were these routed via edge-proxy or direct to regional pop?

alex: edge-proxy -> regional pop -> model. extra hop suspected on US-W. traffic was uniform across regions (1k each) measured over 3m window. overall load ~50 rps.

sam: can you run a direct path (no edge-proxy) for a quick 500-sample check? want to isolate proxy hop + proxy kernel interaction.

jin: also confirm quant profile: int8 symmetric or q4/q8 style? and was KV cache compressed? those change tail behavior.

alex: int8 symmetric, KV-cache enabled, not q4f16. batching=8. kernel pinned to opt-attn-v2. starting a direct-run bypassing edge-proxy now, will flip warmup off for one run too.

ci-bot: Deploy finished: test-run-direct-1745010000 started.

alex: Direct-run results (500 samples):

alex: ```
US-E direct (h100 int8): p50 42ms  p95 115ms
US-W direct (a100 int8): p50 48ms  p95 130ms  <-- big improvement vs proxy
EU-C direct (h100 int8): p50 53ms  p95 135ms
```

maria: interesting — US-W p95 collapses when bypassing the edge. suggests proxy hop + fanout is amplifying tail on a100 path. Could be proxy queuing or kernel handshake.

sam: can we repro with kernel=opt-attn-v1 and with fanout=1? maybe fanout=2 triggers cross-pop coordination on that path.

jin: also try q4f16 profile (lower precision) to see if token compute dominates or network hop dominates. if q4 reduces p95 similarly on proxy path then compute was the bottleneck.

alex: queued: (1) proxy fanout=1, kernel=attn-v1; (2) q4f16 with proxy fanout=2; (3) warmup=off baseline. will post numbers in this thread.

maria: nice. add a quick perf note in the ticket if warmup interacts — we've seen warmup heat reduce p95 by ~20-30% for h100 in previous runs.

jin: filed ticket RW-1234 to track this and include kernel traces + tcp hop counts: https://rwd/tickets/1234 :eyes:

alex: ran fanout=1 + kernel=attn-v1 (proxy). Results:

alex: ```
US-E (proxy, fanout=1, attn-v1): p50 46ms p95 125ms
US-W (proxy, fanout=1, attn-v1): p50 50ms p95 145ms  <-- much closer
EU-C (proxy, fanout=1, attn-v1): p50 56ms p95 142ms
```

sam: ok that points at the fanout behavior interacting badly with US-W path (maybe cross-pop cold connections). Biasing routing to prefer local h100 for that pop seems reasonable until we root-cause.

maria: agree. but also capture quality delta when trying q4f16. we don't want to trade-off regressions for perf.

alex: next run q4f16 (proxy fanout=2). starting now.

alex: q4f16 results (proxy fanout=2):

alex: ```
US-E (q4f16): p50 40ms p95 110ms
US-W (q4f16): p50 46ms p95 135ms
EU-C (q4f16): p50 48ms p95 120ms
```

maria: q4f16 helps overall tail but US-W still shows ~135ms p95 via proxy vs 130ms direct; smaller gap.

sam: action items: (1) route-bias US-W to local h100 for 24h canary; (2) add proxy instrumentation for fanout queuing and connection churn; (3) run a larger q4f16 quality eval against our regression suite.

jin: I'll attach kernel flame traces to RW-1234 and schedule a follow-up deep-dive.

alex: thanks. summary: proxy fanout=2 exacerbates US-W tail on a100 path; bypass or fanout=1 reduces p95; q4f16 reduces tail further. next: canary route-bias + quality eval. :thumbsup:
